text:
maria: Heads up — drift detector just flagged a terraform diff for gpu-quota in eu-west-1. PR #4827 opened by @sam to bump reserved_gpus from 120 -> 160. I didn't approve yet because Conftest failed (freeze window rule).
ci-bot: [auto] drift-detector: terraform plan detected diffs in module/gpu/pool (eu-west-1) at 2026-03-11T10:15:03Z. Link: https://ci.redwood/plan/4827
sam: yep that PR is to support a burst from a customer trial. We have capacity shortfalls on staging and want to pre-provision. I ran plan locally and it looks straightforward.
josh: paste of the conftest error from the pipeline:
```
FAIL: policy/opa/freeze_window.rego: deny[reason]
Reason: "Change blocked: global freeze window active (2026-03-10 to 2026-03-14)"
Resource: aws_quota.gpu_pool.eu_west
```
maria: we're in a company-wide freeze window for infra changes through Sunday. We need either to wait or route through exception flow. This is not an emergency unless prod is impacted.
sam: production isn't impacted, only staging and a customer trial. How long is the exception flow? I can ping sales but wanted to avoid process delay.
josh: exception flow requires two approvers from infra + SRE lead signoff. There's a checkbox in the PR template and you need to set label: infra-exception and include reason + mitigation plan. Ops will triage timeboxed exceptions only.
ops-oncall: @sam if this is business critical, please add the following to the PR body:
- tag: infra-exception
- severity: S2
- rollback plan: terraform apply -target=module.gpu.pools[eu-west] rollback count
- canary: enable 10% capacity in eu-west then monitor for 2 hours
Also paste the pre-run plan output and schedule a quick 15-min review call.
sam: ok adding tag and the canary approach. quick question: can we do a temporary quota bump via provider override (non-gitops) to buy time? Ops allowed that in extreme emergencies.
maria: we try to avoid manual provider overrides. It creates env drift which drift-detector will catch and make the PR noisy later. If you must, coordinate with ops-oncall and mark it emergency_manual on the ticket.
drift-bot: [alert] env-drift job detected manual change in eu-west-1 on 2026-03-11T09:50:12Z. Resource: aws_quota.gpu_pool. Detected by IAM: terraform-bastion. If this is intentional, link PR that will reconcile state.
sam: that manual change was me testing immediate capacity — my bad, forgot to annotate. I'll revert provider override and open the PR properly with exception metadata.
josh: to speed approvals, propose this compromise: merge the PR into a canary branch that Helm charts point to for only the canary pool, and leave main unaffected. That way we can validate autoscaler + networking for extra GPUs without full rollout.
ops-oncall: +1 to canary branch. Also add this Conftest exemption note in PR: `conftest.exemptions: ["capacity-canary-eu-west-2026-03-11"]` and include a short retention note. We'll log the exemption and auto-revoke after 48h.
sam: adding exemption tag and branching strategy now. I included the terraform plan snippet in the PR body:
```
# terraform plan
+ aws_quota.gpu_pool.eu_west
    reserved_gpus: 120 -> 160
```
maria: ping me once PR is updated. I can fast-approve the infra side if ops-oncall signs off and SRE lead confirms canary monitoring (latency, OOM, scheduler failures).
ops-oncall: signed off for a 48h canary window as long as rollback steps are documented. I'll also create an alert runbook for gpu-node-saturation in case the extra capacity triggers autoscaler instability.
sam: thanks. tagging @josh and @maria in the PR and adding the runbook link. scheduling 15-min review at 2026-03-11T11:30Z.
maria: fine to proceed with canary. remind team to not touch provider manual overrides. closing the loop: will watch drift-detector and approve final merge if stable.
ci-bot: [status] PR #4827 updated: labels=[infra-exception, capacity-canary], conftest: exemption added, pipeline re-run queued.
maria: awesome. after canary completes, we do a full gitops rollout and update quota in tfstate. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
